'''''Plantago coronopus''''', the '''buck's-horn plantain''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref>  is a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[Annual plant|annual]] to [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Plantaginaceae]]. Other common names in the US and Italy include '''minutina''' and '''erba stella'''.<ref name=":0" />

==Description==
''Plantago coronopus'' produces a [[Rosette (botany)|basal rosette]] of narrowly lance-shaped leaves up to {{Convert|25|cm|sp=us}} long that are toothed or deeply divided. The [[inflorescence]]s grow erect to about {{Convert abbreviated|4 to 7|cm}} in height. They have dense spikes of flowers which sometimes curve. Each flower has four whitish lobes each measuring about a millimeter long. ''Plantago coronopus'' mainly grows on sandy or gravelly soils close to the sea, but also on salt-treated roadsides.<ref name=BRC>{{cite web|title=Online atlas of the British and Irish flora: Plantago coronopus |publisher=Biological Records Centre and Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/plantago-coronopus |access-date=5 June 2019 }}</ref> It is native to Eurasia and North Africa but it can be found elsewhere, including the United States, Australia, and New Zealand as an [[introduced species]].

It is grown as a [[leaf vegetable]] known as erba stella,<ref name=":0">{{citation |author=Coleman, E. |year=1999  |title=Four-Season Harvest: Organic Vegetables from Your Home Garden All Year Long |publisher=Chelsea Green Publishing |edition=second |isbn=978-1890132279 }}</ref> mostly incorporated in salad mixes for specialty markets. Recently it has become popular as a frost-hardy winter crop for farmers in northern climates, and is usually grown in unheated hightunnels.
